title: Circuit decider oscillation — hosted API chronicle
content:
Summary:

On 2026-12-07 18:14 UTC we observed a sustained increase in 5xx errors and streaming stalls for a subset (~7%) of hosted-API sessions originating from EU-West edge points. The issue lasted ~138 minutes with the worst window between 18:18–19:25 UTC. Impacted customers saw elevated latencies (p50 streaming tail increased by ~3.2s, p99 by ~11s) and intermittent 502/504 errors for non-streaming endpoints. Total served tokens dropped ~5% due to routing fallbacks.

Why this is notable: this incident was not a simple resource exhaustion — it was an oscillation in edge health decisioning that caused frequent host rebalancing and circuit breaker tripping, producing cascading inflight-stream stalls and a large control-plane churn surface. The true root involved an interaction between a recently-merged edge proxy change, an autoscaler flag that had been turned off in a weekend canary, and an unobserved token-bucket parameter mismatch in our circuit-decider logic.

High-level timeline (all times UTC local to logs):
- 18:12:22: Edge health dashboards show slight uptick in in-flight HTTP/2 stream resets in eu-west-1.
- 18:14:03: First PagerDuty noise (SRE rotation) — increased 5xx for /v1/streams from eu-west POP.
- 18:17:50: Streaming latency p50 crosses alert threshold (SRE streaming-latency-eu alert fires).
- 18:20:10: Host router starts marking a subset of backends as unhealthy; per-host circuit-decider counters increment.
- 18:23:45: Autoscaler controller observes imbalance but autoscale evaluation is skipped for affected nodegroups (flag: enable-scale-eu=false in canary config).
- 18:30:00–18:40: Rolling re-routing increases per-host connection churn; streaming sessions degrade and several long-lived streams reset.
- 18:47:02: On-call pushes rollback of last edge-proxy change (PR #921) to canary. Immediate reduction in new unhealthy markings but oscillation persists.
- 19:05:00: Manual increase of circuit-decider thresholds (temporary mitigation) reduces circuit trips; streaming stability improves.
- 19:32:15: Autoscaler flag restored and scale-up allowed, new capacity attaches, full recovery by 19:32–20:30 window as drained sessions reestablish.

Impact metrics (rough):
- Window: 18:14–20:32 UTC
- Affected traffic: ~6–9% of EU-West hosted-API traffic (session affinity skewed to particular edge racks)
- Errors: additional ~42k 5xx responses above baseline; majority 502/504 from upstream resets
- Latency: streaming p99 increased from baseline 1.9s to 13.1s at peak for affected POP
- Customer-facing: 17 customer incidents opened; no long-term data loss reported

How we detected it:
- Primary detection via streaming-latency and edge-reset-rate dashboards.
- SRE on-call pager alarms for p50/p95 increases triggered initial wakeup.
- Correlation in logs showed repeated health-check flaps and host removal decisions originating from the circuit-decider component.

Root cause (in plain terms):
1) Edge proxy change (PR #921 — HTTP/2 window management tweak) altered stream window accounting under heavy prefix-KV cache misses. This change increased the probability of transient stall followed by connection resets for long-lived streams when a host was under modest memory pressure.
2) A separate configuration change in the autoscaler (canary deployment) had disabled EU-West scale evaluations (enable-scale-eu=false). This prevented the quick addition of spare backends when the cluster started seeing more transient failures.
3) Circuit-decider token bucket thresholds had been tuned down in a previous hardening patch to reduce tail latency for small bursts; those thresholds were now too aggressive for the new proxy behavior. The decider started tripping hosts more frequently.
4) The combined result: hosts were repeatedly marked unhealthy and traffic rebalanced; rebalancing caused further KV cache misses and more proxy window pressure, feeding back into the cycle (positive feedback loop).

Why the change interaction was missed in staging:
- The change in PR #921 passed unit tests and the realtime-load smoke tests, but we did not exercise long-lived streaming sessions with large prefix cache miss rates in the canary.
- The autoscaler flag change was pushed as part of a weekend canary roll and not filed as a dependency for the proxy change; monitoring didn’t alert on skipped autoscaler evaluations.
- Circuit-decider threshold tuning occurred weeks ago and did not have a clear changelog entry linking to streaming path sensitivity tests.

Mitigation and remediation performed during incident:
- 18:47:02: Rolled back PR #921 from the canary edge ring (partial mitigation for new sessions).
- 19:05:00: Temporarily relaxed circuit-decider trip thresholds to stop aggressive host evacuation. This was a config push to edge-config that reduced circuit trips by ~80%.
- 19:20:00: Restored autoscaler evaluation flag (enable-scale-eu=true) and forced a scale evaluation, which allowed new nodes to join and absorb load.
- 19:32:15: Gradual reintroduction of PR #921 after we tuned window-accounting parameters in the proxy (smaller delta, additional guard rails).

Remediation plan (short term):
- Reproduce locally and in a dedicated stress canary: create an automated harness that runs long-lived HTTP/2 streaming sessions with artificial KV-cache miss injection to simulate worst-case coupling. (owner: Arun, due 2026-12-14)
- Add an end-to-end canary test that includes autoscaler evaluation checks after control-plane changes; block merges if canary flag suppression is detected. (owner: Sofia, due 2026-12-18)
- Revert the more aggressive circuit-decider thresholds in prod and adopt conservative defaults; new defaults should be annotated with observed safe ranges. (owner: Maya, done 2026-12-09)
- Add telemetry for "scale-eval-skipped" events and a high-priority alert when scale evaluations are suppressed for >5 minutes in a region. (owner: Liam, due 2026-12-17)

Remediation plan (longer term):
- Migrate critical streaming health checks into the control plane so that router decisions consider long-lived stream health (not just short-liveness probes). (owner: eng-serving-runtime, roadmap Q1 2027)
- Implement a canary policy dependency graph so that config flags and proxy changes that interact must be signaled together and held in the same canary ring. (owner: platform-engineering, roadmap Q2 2027)
- Rework circuit-decider to incorporate hysteresis and adaptive thresholds based on observed KV miss-rate and in-flight stream count, not purely token-bucket. (owner: serving-runtime, design doc by 2027-03-01)

Runbook and monitoring updates (immediate):
- Update runbook "edge-health-decision-playbook" with a new checklist: check autoscaler flags, query circuit-decider counters, correlate with KV-cache miss rate and long-lived stream resets. (doc owners: SRE)
- Add dashboard tile: region-level scale-eval-suppressed, with 1m/5m pace and alerted if >5 minutes.
- Add a lightweight synthetic long-lived-stream canary per region that reports: steady-state throughput, window-backpressure incidents, and reset count every 30s.

Action items (concrete):
- [DONE] Relax circuit-decider thresholds (Maya) — temporary but stays until conservative defaults roll out.
- [IN PROGRESS] Long-lived-stream stress harness (Arun) — infra standing up in canary cluster.
- [TODO] Add scale-eval suppression alert (Liam).
- [TODO] Post-rollback audit of PR #921 to isolate exact delta causing window pressure and rework. (owner: edge-proxy team)

Open questions / notes to self:
- We need a clear tagging/labelling convention for weekend canaries vs normal canaries; control-plane config flips should be visible in the merge checklist.
- Could we add a pre-merge lint that checks for disabled autoscaler flags in any region? This would have blocked the hidden dependency that increased risk.
- How often do we simulate cache miss storms in staging? Frequency seems insufficient. Plan: weekly scheduled miss-storm runs in canary.

Post-incident lessons learned (summary):
- Small, unrelated changes can interact nonlinearly; we need to treat autoscaler control-plane flags as high-risk config.
- Long-lived streaming workloads require end-to-end canaries that exercise the full stack and KV-cache dynamics.
- Circuit breakers and token buckets are brittle without context: they must incorporate environment signals (cache miss rate, in-flight stream ratio) or they will amplify failure modes.

Appendix (logs & quick notes):
- Useful queries: 
  - edge-proxy logs: filter by http2.window_event and upstream_reset with tag eu-west-1
  - circuit-decider: counter:host_trips{region="eu-west-1",ring="canary"} by 1m
  - autoscaler: events where scale_evaluation_skipped=true in last 60m

- Quick command that helped during incident: curl -H "X-Canary-Check: stream" https://internal-canary/eu-west/longstream - ran simple synthetic long stream to see immediate backpressure metrics on candidate hosts.

Owner signoff: Maya Chen (SRE lead) — draft for review by eng-serving-runtime and edge-proxy teams.
